summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a history of HCV and alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatic encephalopathy, and major depression was admitted for abdominal pain, confusion, and lactic acidosis. She was somnolent on arrival, with asterixis and elevated lactate of 6.2, consistent with hepatic encephalopathy and volume depletion. CT imaging showed resolving colitis with new cecal thickening, suggesting recurrent infectious colitis. She was treated with IV fluids, IV antibiotics, and frequent lactulose, with rapid improvement in mental status and lactate normalization. Her tachycardia resolved, and she was transitioned to oral antibiotics. Stool studies were negative for pathogens. She regained baseline mental function, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home on a full course of antibiotics, with instructions to continue lactulose, avoid alcohol, and follow up with care services.
